verdict.rationale: Lium documents Volumes as storage that outlives pods: a volume attaches to a pod at /mnt and keeps its data after the pod is deleted, which covers the core of the story. The evidence does not say volumes are network-attached, or that one volume can be reattached to a different node or later rental, so the 'outlives any single GPU rental' part is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit network-attached storage semantics, documented reattachment of a volume to new pods on other nodes, size and region limits, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attach persistent network storage that survives instance teardown, so datasets and checkpoints outlive any single GPU rental

citations.quote: A **Volume** is storage that outlives your pods. Attach one to a pod and it is mounted at **`/mnt`**.
It keeps your data after the pod is deleted.
Click **COST HISTORY** for the last 30 days, per volume per day.
